notes: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Japanese Studies Students is a national government scholarship administered by MEXT via embassy recommendation. Recipients study in the one-year 'Japanese Studies Program' course at one of the designated Japanese universities listed in the Course Guide, chosen at MEXT/embassy allocation. No single institution or supervising professor is attached to the scholarship itself, and the official guidelines PDF (verified live, HTTP 200, PDF binary) names only the programme, not staff. Per research guidance, national/government schemes such as MEXT resolve to not_applicable.

JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students is a national stipend administered by the Japan Student Services Organization (JASSO). It is not open to direct application: each host educational institution nominates candidates, with quotas based on the institution's international enrolment. Verified live at https://www.jasso.go.jp/en/ryugaku/scholarship_j/index.html, which states JASSO 'provides the following financial assistance' and lists the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship with no named faculty. No institution or professor is attached to the scholarship, so not_applicable.

JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan (Standard Program) is a national research fellowship run by the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science. Verified live at https://www.jsps.go.jp/english/e-fellow/e-ippan/appliguidelines.html: the FY2027 open call shows a 'Application deadline (from host institution to JSPS)' column, 120 fellowships per round, and a single central contact 'Overseas Fellowship Division, International Program Department, Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) ... postdoc-standard*jsps.go.jp'. There is no named supervising professor or attached institution; the applicant chooses and works with a host researcher who is not published as part of the award, so not_applicable.

JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term Program (PE), Open Call is a national research fellowship run by JSPS. Verified live at https://www.jsps.go.jp/english/e-fellow/e-oubei-s/appliguidelines.html: the FY2027 schedule lists three rounds, 20 fellowships each, with applications submitted 'from host institution to JSPS'. Contact is the central JSPS Overseas Fellowship Division (postdoc-short*jsps.go.jp). Eligible countries are restricted (US, Canada, EU, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Russia). No named supervising professor or attached institution, so not_applicable.

JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term (FY2027, 2nd Recruitment) is a national invitation fellowship administered by JSPS. Verified live at https://www.jsps.go.jp/english/e-inv/application/index.html: FY2027 rounds run 14-60 day (short-term) visits with application deadlines of 28 August 2026 (1st) and 23 April 2027 (2nd), submitted by the host institution to JSPS. The only published contact is the central JSPS Overseas Fellowship Division (invitation*jsps.go.jp). No named host researcher or attached institution is published as part of the award, so not_applicable.

Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Scholarship for Overseas Candidates is a private foundation scholarship administered by the Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Foundation, not tied to any one institution. Verified live at https://www.rotary-yoneyama.or.jp/english/overseas: 'Applicants have to find out and apply for Japanese universities / graduate schools by themselves before applying for this scholarship' and 'Those who enroll in graduate schools are requested to submit a recommendation letter from a supervisor / professor of the applicants' targeted graduate school.' Because the target university and supervisor are chosen freely by each applicant and are not attached to the award, no professor can be verified, so not_applicable.

The NL Scholarship is the Dutch national scholarship programme financed by the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with participating Dutch higher education institutions, and is not attached to a single institution. Verified live at https://www.studyinnl.org/finances/nl-scholarship: 'This scholarship is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science as well as several Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences.' It lists 11 participating research universities and 25 universities of applied sciences for 2026-2027 and states 'You meet the specific requirements of the institution of your choice. You can find these on the website of the institution.' Because the participating-institution list changes annually and no single programme/faculty is attached, this is a national scheme, so not_applicable.
